g5: artifact-manifest — a run-level index records every group's output, and `run` entries reach downstream prompts

u6: New `execution/artifacts.py` holds `ArtifactEntry`/`ArtifactManifest` and an atomic, lock-guarded store at `RunPaths.artifact_manifest_path` (`<run_dir>/artifacts.json`); `code` groups register an entry on merge and a `partial` one on Resolve; a coder whose direct upstream groups are non-`code` gets their entries (never file bodies) folded into its first prompt.

Plan section U6

U6. artifact-manifest — a run-level index records every group's output, and run entries reach downstream prompts

  • Summary: New execution/artifacts.py holds ArtifactEntry/ArtifactManifest and an atomic, lock-guarded store at RunPaths.artifact_manifest_path (<run_dir>/artifacts.json); code groups register an entry on merge and a partial one on Resolve; a coder whose direct upstream groups are non-code gets their entries (never file bodies) folded into its first prompt.
  • Goal: ArtifactEntry carries artifact_id, group_id, tasks, recipe, paths, sha256 (per file, for files that exist), commit (merge commit or None), schema (the contract model's name), summary (≤ 2,000 chars, required), status (complete | partial), measurements (dict[str, scalar], empty for code), recorded_at. register(entry) is idempotent per artifact_id (a re-merge replaces, never duplicates). MergeLadder._merge registers a complete code entry after a successful merge_group (summary = the final CoderReport.summary; paths = git diff --name-only between the group's base and its merge commit — what actually changed, not the declared Group.files; commit = the merge sha, and the per-file sha256 map stays empty for code, since git already content-addresses every file at that commit); the scheduler registers a partial entry when a group lands RESOLVED. A new _apply_artifact_inputs (declared in host.py, called where the first coder prompt is built in generation.py) appends one block listing each non-code direct-upstream entry, in dependency order, capped at 8,000 characters in total — measurements are truncated first, with a +N more — see artifacts.json line; the block is appended to the first coder prompt and to every fresh generation's handoff prompt (the self.handoff_prompt or render_coder_prompt(...) site, generation.py:225), because a retired generation has lost all context. With no such upstream, every prompt is unchanged byte-for-byte.
  • Files: orchestrator/execution/artifacts.py (new, medium), orchestrator/execution/manifest.py, orchestrator/execution/merge_ladder.py, orchestrator/execution/generation.py, orchestrator/execution/host.py, orchestrator/execution/scheduler.py, tests/test_artifact_manifest.py (new, medium)
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: U3
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: implements ArtifactManifest; consumes Group.recipe
  • Verification:
    • After a tests/test_review_loop.py-harness run of two code groups (real git worktrees), artifacts.json holds two complete code entries whose commit values each resolve with git cat-file -t <sha> → commit in that repo.
    • A group resolved from Stranded Work produces an entry with status == "partial".
    • A code group downstream of a run group gets a first prompt containing the run entry's artifact_id, summary and measurements and none of the output files' bytes; a code group downstream only of code groups gets a first prompt byte-identical to one built before this change.
    • An entry with a 2,001-char summary is rejected at register naming summary.
    • A code group downstream of a run entry with 300 measurement keys gets an injected block ≤ 8,000 characters ending in a +N more — see artifacts.json line.
    • A downstream coder retired by the breaker and relaunched as generation 2 gets the same upstream-entries block in its handoff prompt.
  • Edge cases:
    • Breaker retirement and relaunch: the upstream-entries block rides every fresh generation's prompt, not only generation 1.
    • A group that touched files outside its declared files is indexed by what it actually changed (diff at merge).
  • Non-goals / must-not: —

orchestrator/execution/artifacts.py
@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
1"""The run-level Artifact Manifest (plan U6): a single index of what every
2group produced, fed to downstream prompts and additive on the Run Bundle.
3
4A ``code`` entry is written by the orchestrator at merge time from data it
5already has (the merge commit, the files the diff actually touched, the
6final ``CoderReport.summary``) — the coder's own prompt and report are
7untouched by this module. A ``run`` recipe entry (a later plan) registers
8through the same store. Only non-``code`` entries are ever injected into a
9downstream prompt (see ``render_artifact_inputs_block``); a ``code`` entry
10exists for the Run Bundle and for a human reading ``artifacts.json``.
11"""
12
13from __future__ import annotations
14
15import threading
16from collections.abc import Sequence
17from datetime import UTC, datetime
18from typing import Literal
19
20from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
21
22from orchestrator.execution.manifest import RunPaths, atomic_write_text
23
24#: R16's cap on an entry's summary — validated here, never truncated later.
25ARTIFACT_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS = 2000
26
27#: Total size of the block folded into a downstream coder's prompt (Goal):
28#: measurements are truncated first, ending in a "+N more" line, before an
29#: entry itself would ever be dropped.
30ARTIFACT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS = 8000
31
32Measurement = float | int | str | bool
33
34
35class ArtifactEntry(BaseModel):
36 """One group's registered output. ``schema`` (aliased — the bare name
37 shadows ``BaseModel``) names the contract model this entry's shape
38 follows (``"CoderReport"`` for every ``code`` entry today)."""
39
40 model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)
41
42 artifact_id: str
43 group_id: str
44 tasks: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
45 recipe: str
46 paths: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
47 #: Per-file content hash, for files that exist. Empty for ``code`` —
48 #: git already content-addresses every file at ``commit``.
49 sha256: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
50 commit: str | None = None
51 schema_name: str = Field(alias="schema")
52 summary: str = Field(max_length=ARTIFACT_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS)
53 status: Literal["complete", "partial"]
54 measurements: dict[str, Measurement] = Field(default_factory=dict)
55 recorded_at: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC).isoformat())
56
57
58class ArtifactManifest(BaseModel):
59 """The content of ``artifacts.json``: every entry, keyed by ``artifact_id``."""
60
61 entries: dict[str, ArtifactEntry] = Field(default_factory=dict)
62
63
64class ArtifactManifestStore:
65 """Load/save the run's Artifact Manifest, guarded by a process-local lock
66 so concurrent groups merging at once cannot tear a load-modify-save."""
67
68 def __init__(self, paths: RunPaths):
69 self.paths = paths
70 self._lock = threading.Lock()
71
72 def load(self) -> ArtifactManifest:
73 path = self.paths.artifact_manifest_path
74 if not path.is_file():
75 return ArtifactManifest()
76 return ArtifactManifest.model_validate_json(path.read_text())
77
78 def save(self, manifest: ArtifactManifest) -> None:
79 atomic_write_text(
80 self.paths.artifact_manifest_path,
81 manifest.model_dump_json(indent=2, by_alias=True) + "\n",
82 )
83
84 def register(self, entry: ArtifactEntry) -> None:
85 """Idempotent per ``artifact_id``: a re-merge (or a Resolve settling
86 a group the same run already registered once) replaces the entry
87 rather than duplicating it."""
88 with self._lock:
89 manifest = self.load()
90 manifest.entries[entry.artifact_id] = entry
91 self.save(manifest)
92
93 def get(self, artifact_id: str) -> ArtifactEntry | None:
94 return self.load().entries.get(artifact_id)
95
96
97def _format_measurement(value: Measurement) -> str:
98 return str(value)
99
100
101def render_artifact_inputs_block(entries: Sequence[ArtifactEntry]) -> str:
102 """The block folded into a downstream coder's prompt (Goal): each
103 upstream entry's id, summary and measurements, in the given order, never
104 its ``paths`` or file bytes. Capped at ``ARTIFACT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS``
105 total — measurements are truncated first, per entry, ending in a
106 "``+N more — see artifacts.json``" line. Empty input renders "" so a
107 prompt with no non-``code`` upstream is unchanged byte-for-byte."""
108 if not entries:
109 return ""
110 close_line = "+0 more — see artifacts.json\n"
111 reserve = len(close_line)
112 parts: list[str] = ["## Upstream artifacts\n\n"]
113 total = len(parts[0])
114 for entry in entries:
115 header = f"### {entry.artifact_id} (group {entry.group_id})\n{entry.summary}\n"
116 measurement_items = sorted(entry.measurements.items())
117 kept_lines: list[str] = []
118 remaining = list(measurement_items)
119 if remaining:
120 header += "Measurements:\n"
121 budget_before_measurements = total + len(header)
122 while remaining:
123 key, value = remaining[0]
124 line = f"- {key}: {_format_measurement(value)}\n"
125 projected = budget_before_measurements + sum(len(x) for x in kept_lines) + len(line)
126 if projected + reserve > ARTIFACT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS:
127 break
128 kept_lines.append(line)
129 remaining.pop(0)
130 entry_text = header + "".join(kept_lines)
131 if remaining:
132 entry_text += f"+{len(remaining)} more — see artifacts.json\n"
133 entry_text += "\n"
134 if total + len(entry_text) > ARTIFACT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS and parts[1:]:
135 # This whole entry cannot fit alongside what is already kept —
136 # stop rather than silently drop it mid-entry.
137 break
138 parts.append(entry_text)
139 total += len(entry_text)
140 return "".join(parts).rstrip() + "\n"

154 def _upstream_artifact_entries(self) -> list[ArtifactEntry]:
155 """Registered entries for every direct upstream group whose recipe is
156 not `code`, in `Group.dependencies` order (plan U6 Goal). Empty when
157 no Artifact Manifest is wired (`deps.artifacts is None`, every
158 construction site that predates this unit) or none of the group's
159 direct upstreams is a non-`code` recipe."""
160 store = self.deps.artifacts
161 if store is None:
162 return []
163 entries: list[ArtifactEntry] = []
164 for dep_id in self.group.dependencies:
165 upstream = self.deps.groups_by_id.get(dep_id)
166 if upstream is None or upstream.recipe == "code":
167 continue
168 entry = store.get(dep_id)
169 if entry is not None:
170 entries.append(entry)
171 return entries

173 def _apply_artifact_inputs(self, prompt: str) -> str:
174 """Fold non-`code` direct upstreams' Artifact Manifest entries into
175 `prompt` (plan U6 Goal). A no-op — byte-identical `prompt` — when
176 there is nothing to fold in, so a code-only plan's prompts are
177 unchanged."""
178 block = render_artifact_inputs_block(self._upstream_artifact_entries())
179 if not block:
180 return prompt
181 return f"{prompt}\n\n{block}"

g6: bundle-additive — the Run Bundle exports the Artifact Manifest and the `runner` role without a version bump

u7: `export` writes the Artifact Manifest as a new optional top-level `artifact_manifest` key (index only, never output bytes) and exports `run` triage calls as `llm_calls` rows with `operation: "run_triage"`; `schema_version` stays 2; the contract doc and the Observatory's `SessionRole` type learn the `runner` label.

Plan section U7

U7. bundle-additive — the Run Bundle exports the Artifact Manifest and the runner role without a version bump

  • Summary: export writes the Artifact Manifest as a new optional top-level artifact_manifest key (index only, never output bytes) and exports run triage calls as llm_calls rows with operation: "run_triage"; schema_version stays 2; the contract doc and the Observatory's SessionRole type learn the runner label.
  • Goal: ExportBundle (the ingest.json model in export.py) gains artifact_manifest: list[ExportManifestEntry] | None, absent when the run has no artifacts.json — a new model name, because ExportArtifact (export.py:100) already means a group's coder-report/reviewer-verdict files and keeps that meaning. The bundle carries the index only (paths, sha256, commit, measurements, summary, status), never copies of output files. A run triage call is recorded by JsonlCallRecorder like the rewrite speccer, so it exports through the existing llm_calls path (ExportLlmCall, _llm_calls at export.py:529) with operation == "run_triage" and group_ids == [gid], carrying its tokens and transcript events; runner is the role label of the Observatory snapshot's synthetic per-group row for it, as rewrites appear as orchestrator rows today. Nothing is double-counted: no SessionEntry is created for a triage call. docs/run-bundle-contract.md documents the key, the entry fields, and the new role value under the additive-change rule. ui/src/types.ts SessionRole adds "runner", and the UI's role-dependent code (attempts.ts, cost.ts) treats an unknown or runner role without throwing.
  • Files: orchestrator/execution/export.py, docs/run-bundle-contract.md, ui/src/types.ts, ui/src/attempts.ts, tests/test_export.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: U6
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: consumes ArtifactManifest
  • Verification:
    • Run (driver): from the main checkout (.orchestrator/runs/ is gitignored and absent in a worktree), uv run smart-mcps-orchestrate export r20260923-163956 --out <scratch dir> — Pass: it succeeds, and ingest.json has schema_version == 2 and no artifact_manifest key (additive: old runs export unchanged).
    • A run directory with an artifacts.json and an llm/calls.json holding a run_triage call exports both — the entries under artifact_manifest, the call under llm_calls with operation == "run_triage" and its group id — and the bundle validates against the models in export.py; the existing per-group artifacts (report/verdict) list is unchanged.
    • npm --prefix ui run build (which runs tsc) and npm --prefix ui test pass, including a test rendering a group whose snapshot carries a synthetic runner row.
  • Edge cases: —
  • Non-goals / must-not:
    • Copying run outputs into ingest/ — the bundle indexes them; consumers open the files where they live.

266### `ExportManifestEntry` (the Artifact Manifest, one per registered output)
267
268The top-level `artifact_manifest` key (added in `schema_version` 2,
269additively — see [Versioning rule](#versioning-rule)) is the run-level index
270of what every group produced (plan U6/U7): the paths, hashes and a human
271summary, never the output files' own bytes — a consumer opens the files where
272they live, using `paths` as pointers. **The key is absent entirely, not set
273to `null`, on a run with no `artifacts.json`** (every run before plan U6),
274so an old run's `ingest.json` is byte-for-byte what it always was. When
275present, it is a flat list, sorted by `artifact_id`.
276
277| field | type | null-tolerance |
278| -------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
279| `artifact_id` | string | always present |
280| `group_id` | string | always present |
281| `tasks` | string[] | `[]` if the entry names none |
282| `recipe` | string | the group's recipe (`"code"` or `"run"` today) |
283| `paths` | string[] | relative to the run's repo root; `[]` for an entry with nothing on disk |
284| `sha256` | `Record<string, string>` | one hash per path that exists; `{}` for `code` — git already content-addresses every file at `commit` |
285| `commit` | string \| null | null when the entry recorded no commit |
286| `schema` | string | the contract model the entry's shape follows (`"CoderReport"` for a `code` entry) |
287| `summary` | string | capped at 2000 characters at write time, never truncated by the exporter |
288| `status` | string | `"complete"` \| `"partial"` — `"partial"` for a Resolve settling unfinished work |
289| `measurements` | `Record<string, number \| string \| boolean>` | `{}` if the recipe recorded none |
290| `recorded_at` | string (ISO 8601) | always present |
291
292A `code` group's entry is written by the orchestrator at merge time from data
293it already has; a `run` group's entry is written by that recipe's own
294executor. Both are index-only — copying an output's bytes into the bundle is
295explicitly out of scope for this key.
296

829def _artifact_manifest(paths: RunPaths) -> list[ExportManifestEntry] | None:
830 """The run's Artifact Manifest, index only. ``None`` when the run has no
831 ``artifacts.json`` at all (every run before plan U6) — an unreadable or
832 malformed file degrades the same way, on the same "the audit trail is
833 inert by contract" rule ``_llm_calls`` follows, rather than failing an
834 otherwise-whole bundle."""

838 manifest = ArtifactManifestStore(paths).load()

843 ExportManifestEntry(
844 artifact_id=entry.artifact_id,
845 group_id=entry.group_id,
846 tasks=list(entry.tasks),
847 recipe=entry.recipe,
848 paths=list(entry.paths),
849 sha256=dict(entry.sha256),
850 commit=entry.commit,
851 schema=entry.schema_name,
852 summary=entry.summary,
853 status=entry.status,
854 measurements=dict(entry.measurements),
855 recorded_at=entry.recorded_at,
856 )
857 for entry in entries
858 ]

g7: run-recipe — the `run` executor runs declared commands as confined, re-adoptable Run Children and records what happened

u8: New `execution/run_child.py` (launch wrapper, per-attempt state, re-adoption, wall-clock cap) and `execution/run_executor.py` (the `run` recipe's executor: worktree, commands in order, measurements, porcelain check against `commit_paths`, commit + `merge_group`, `RunRecord` validation, Artifact Manifest entry, one-shot triage on failure); `confinement.build_policy` gains an `extra_write` parameter.

Plan section U8

U8. run-recipe — the run executor runs declared commands as confined, re-adoptable Run Children and records what happened

  • Summary: New execution/run_child.py (launch wrapper, per-attempt state, re-adoption, wall-clock cap) and execution/run_executor.py (the run recipe's executor: worktree, commands in order, measurements, porcelain check against commit_paths, commit + merge_group, RunRecord validation, Artifact Manifest entry, one-shot triage on failure); confinement.build_policy gains an extra_write parameter.
  • Goal: For each command in order, the executor launches a wrapper that runs the command and records its exit status in <attempt>/<n>.exit — by default sh -c 'sh -c "$1"; rc=$?; echo "$rc" > "$2.tmp" && mv "$2.tmp" "$2"' sh <cmd> <exit file>, the command passed as a positional argument and never interpolated into the wrapper text, the exit file written atomically, a signal-killed command recording 128+n — with cwd = the group worktree (or the declared cwd inside it), start_new_session=True, stdout/stderr to <attempt>/<n>.out/.err, and preexec_fn from landlock_preexec(build_policy(worktree, …, extra_write=data_layer_write_paths + allow_write)). It records {n, pid, starttime, cmdline_head, started_at, started_monotonic, boot_id} in groups/<gid>/run/attempt-<k>/state.json — never in live_pids. It polls (exit detected by default via os.pidfd_open + poll, which works for a process this orchestrator did not fork; the exit status always comes from the exit file); the RoundHeartbeat phase reads command n/N · elapsed/cap · +bytes. The cap measures awake time: elapsed = time.monotonic() − started_monotonic (Linux CLOCK_MONOTONIC excludes suspend and is system-wide within one boot, so it stays valid across an orchestrator restart); /proc starttime and /proc/uptime are boot-time clocks that include suspend and are not used for the cap. On exceeding wall_clock_min it sends SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL after a grace period, and treats the command as timed out. On start, if the latest attempt's state names a pid that _is_same_process confirms and whose /proc/<pid>/stat state is not Z (an exited-but-unreaped process still matches on start time) and the boot_id is unchanged, it re-adopts that child; if the pid is gone (or a zombie) with no exit file, the command counts as "died with the orchestrator". A deliberate stop — Ctrl-C, Observatory Stop, RunAbort, i.e. the executor's task being cancelled — kills the Run Child's process group before the orchestrator exits; only an unclean death (kill -9, OOM, power loss) leaves it running for resume to re-adopt. A retry starts attempt k+1 from the first command that did not exit 0 in attempt k; a retry note containing --from-start reruns every command. After all commands exit 0, every declared outputs path must exist — a missing one goes to triage; it then reads the measurements file (top-level scalars) — a missing or unparsable measurements file never fails the unit (P2): the entry completes with a measurements_missing note; then it runs git status --porcelain: paths outside commit_paths fail the unit naming them; matches are committed and merged via deps.merge_group. It builds a RunRecord, validates it (a validation error names the field), registers a complete run entry (summary generated from exit codes, durations, measurements) and returns COMPLETED. Any non-zero exit, timeout, porcelain violation, PreflightFailure or MergeConflict goes to deps.triage once: work_failure → FAILED with the diagnosis in the group failure and run.log; needs_decision → an escalation via the broker (or FAILED when HITL is off). It never relaunches itself; no reviewer session ever runs.
  • Files: orchestrator/execution/run_child.py (new, medium), orchestrator/execution/run_executor.py (new, large), orchestrator/execution/confinement.py, orchestrator/prompts/run_triage.md (new, small), tests/test_run_child.py (new, medium), tests/test_run_executor.py (new, large)
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: U1, U5, U6
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: consumes UnitRecipe, executor-dispatch, ArtifactManifest
  • Verification:
    • A real run group whose command is python -c writing {"score": 0.9} to a data_dirs path completes: artifacts.json has a run entry with measurements == {"score": 0.9}, the output file's sha256, and exit status 0; no SessionEntry of role coder or reviewer exists for the group.
    • A command sleep 30 with wall_clock_min set to 0.05 is killed (its process group no longer exists per /proc) and triage is called once with a timed-out status.
    • Re-adoption: start a sleep 20 Run Child, drop the executor (simulated crash), construct a new executor for the same group; it re-adopts the same pid (no second sleep process appears in /proc) and completes when the child exits.
    • Confinement, real kernel, worker-runnable: with build_policy(..., system_paths=[]) over three fresh tmp_path directories — worktree, data dir, and an allow_write extra — plus a fourth undeclared one, a Run Child on a host where landlock_abi_version() > 0 writes into the first three and fails to write into the fourth (a narrower profile than the worker's own, so the test proves the child's rules even inside a confined worker).
    • Run (driver): the same probe against the real home directory — Pass: a Run Child writing $HOME/.claude/projects/<another project's slug>/probe fails, and a declared allow_write path outside the worker profile (for example ~/.cache/run-recipe-probe/) becomes writable. Driver-only: a confined worker can neither observe that denial as the child's (it is already denied itself) nor grant a path it cannot write.
    • A command that edits a tracked file outside commit_paths fails the unit, and the failure names that path.
    • Run (driver): kill -9 the run process mid-command on a real run of a fixture plan with a 2-minute sleep command, then uv run smart-mcps-orchestrate resume <run_id> — Pass: run.log shows the child re-adopted (same pid), the group completes, and exactly one sleep process ever existed.
    • Awake-time cap: with the monotonic clock patched to exclude a simulated 8-hour gap in wall time, a command with a 60-minute cap that has run 20 awake minutes is not killed; a changed boot_id in the attempt state makes a recorded pid unadoptable.
    • Stop kills, crash keeps: cancelling the executor's task mid-command leaves no process of the Run Child's group in /proc; dropping the executor without cancellation (simulated crash) leaves the child running.
    • Retry resumes: after an attempt where command 2 of 3 exits 1, retry runs only commands 2 and 3 (command 1 is never relaunched); the same retry with a note containing --from-start runs all three.
    • A command containing single quotes, a pipe and an env prefix (FOO='a b' sh -c 'echo "$FOO"' | tr a-z A-Z > out) runs exactly as written, and its exit file holds 0.
    • A command that exits 0 but never writes a declared outputs path goes to triage; one whose declared measurements file is absent completes with measurements_missing in its entry.
  • Edge cases:
    • Laptop suspend during a command: the cap counts awake time only; an overnight suspend does not kill a half-done render on wake.
    • A Run Child that exited while no orchestrator was alive is a zombie until PID 1 reaps it; state Z counts as exited, never as re-adoptable.
    • Retry after partial success skips commands that already exited 0 unless the retry note says --from-start.
    • Ctrl-C or Observatory Stop kills the Run Child's process group; only an unclean orchestrator death leaves it for re-adoption.
    • A command that itself calls setsid or setpgid escapes the process-group kill; the timeout kill cannot reach it, and the triage diagnosis says so when a timed-out command's output shows it.
  • Non-goals / must-not:
    • The launch/re-adopt mechanics named above (positional-argument wrapper, tmp+mv exit file, pidfd_open+poll, zombie check) are defaults, not mandates: a worker that hits a surprise may substitute a different mechanism, provided the verification outcomes above still hold and the substitution is reported as a surprise with its reason.

U8. run-recipe — the run executor runs declared commands as confined, re-adoptable Run Children and records what happened

  • Summary: New execution/run_child.py (launch wrapper, per-attempt state, re-adoption, wall-clock cap) and execution/run_executor.py (the run recipe's executor: worktree, commands in order, measurements, porcelain check against commit_paths, commit + merge_group, RunRecord validation, Artifact Manifest entry, one-shot triage on failure); confinement.build_policy gains an extra_write parameter.
  • Goal: For each command in order, the executor launches a wrapper that runs the command and records its exit status in <attempt>/<n>.exit — by default sh -c 'sh -c "$1"; rc=$?; echo "$rc" > "$2.tmp" && mv "$2.tmp" "$2"' sh <cmd> <exit file>, the command passed as a positional argument and never interpolated into the wrapper text, the exit file written atomically, a signal-killed command recording 128+n — with cwd = the group worktree (or the declared cwd inside it), start_new_session=True, stdout/stderr to <attempt>/<n>.out/.err, and preexec_fn from landlock_preexec(build_policy(worktree, …, extra_write=data_layer_write_paths + allow_write)). It records {n, pid, starttime, cmdline_head, started_at, started_monotonic, boot_id} in groups/<gid>/run/attempt-<k>/state.json — never in live_pids. It polls (exit detected by default via os.pidfd_open + poll, which works for a process this orchestrator did not fork; the exit status always comes from the exit file); the RoundHeartbeat phase reads command n/N · elapsed/cap · +bytes. The cap measures awake time: elapsed = time.monotonic() − started_monotonic (Linux CLOCK_MONOTONIC excludes suspend and is system-wide within one boot, so it stays valid across an orchestrator restart); /proc starttime and /proc/uptime are boot-time clocks that include suspend and are not used for the cap. On exceeding wall_clock_min it sends SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL after a grace period, and treats the command as timed out. On start, if the latest attempt's state names a pid that _is_same_process confirms and whose /proc/<pid>/stat state is not Z (an exited-but-unreaped process still matches on start time) and the boot_id is unchanged, it re-adopts that child; if the pid is gone (or a zombie) with no exit file, the command counts as "died with the orchestrator". A deliberate stop — Ctrl-C, Observatory Stop, RunAbort, i.e. the executor's task being cancelled — kills the Run Child's process group before the orchestrator exits; only an unclean death (kill -9, OOM, power loss) leaves it running for resume to re-adopt. A retry starts attempt k+1 from the first command that did not exit 0 in attempt k; a retry note containing --from-start reruns every command. After all commands exit 0, every declared outputs path must exist — a missing one goes to triage; it then reads the measurements file (top-level scalars) — a missing or unparsable measurements file never fails the unit (P2): the entry completes with a measurements_missing note; then it runs git status --porcelain: paths outside commit_paths fail the unit naming them; matches are committed and merged via deps.merge_group. It builds a RunRecord, validates it (a validation error names the field), registers a complete run entry (summary generated from exit codes, durations, measurements) and returns COMPLETED. Any non-zero exit, timeout, porcelain violation, PreflightFailure or MergeConflict goes to deps.triage once: work_failure → FAILED with the diagnosis in the group failure and run.log; needs_decision → an escalation via the broker (or FAILED when HITL is off). It never relaunches itself; no reviewer session ever runs.

orchestrator/execution/run_child.py
@@ -0,0 +1,248 @@
1"""Run Child launch, re-adoption and wall-clock cap mechanics (plan U8).
2
3A Run Child is a detached subprocess (``start_new_session=True``) launched
4through a positional-argument wrapper so the command text is never
5interpolated into a shell script: ``sh -c 'sh -c "$1"; rc=$?; echo "$rc" >
6"$2.tmp" && mv "$2.tmp" "$2"' sh <cmd> <exit_file>``. Its exit status is
7read from that exit file, written atomically (write-then-rename), never from
8this process's own ``wait()`` — a re-adopted child was never our fork child,
9so we cannot ``wait()`` it at all.
10
11Re-adoption identifies the *same* process the way the scheduler already does
12for worker subprocesses (``_is_same_process`` in ``scheduler.py``): the
13kernel process start time (field 22 of ``/proc/<pid>/stat``) must match, and
14argv[0]'s basename must match. On top of that a Run Child also checks the
15recorded ``boot_id`` (a pid + start time pair can theoretically recur across
16a reboot on a long-lived host) and that ``/proc/<pid>/stat``'s state is not
17``Z`` — a zombie has exited but not yet been reaped by PID 1, and counts as
18gone, not adoptable.
19
20The wall-clock cap measures **awake** time (``time.monotonic()`` deltas),
21never a ``/proc``-derived boot-time clock, so a laptop suspend does not count
22against a long render (deepen edge case).
23"""
24
25from __future__ import annotations
26
27import ctypes
28import os
29import select
30import signal
31import subprocess
32import time
33from collections.abc import Callable
34from pathlib import Path
35
36from pydantic import BaseModel
37
38_LIBC = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
39_LIBC.syscall.restype = ctypes.c_long
40
41# x86_64 syscall number; pidfd_open landed in Linux 5.3.
42_SYS_PIDFD_OPEN = 434
43
44DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 1.0
45DEFAULT_KILL_GRACE_S = 5.0
46
47
48class RunChildState(BaseModel):
49 """What is persisted to ``attempt-<k>/<n>.state.json`` at launch — never
50 to ``live_pids``, which is the worker-subprocess registry the scheduler
51 reaps unconditionally on a crashed-orchestrator restart."""
52
53 n: int
54 pid: int
55 starttime: str | None = None
56 cmdline_head: str | None = None
57 started_at: str
58 started_monotonic: float
59 boot_id: str | None = None
60
61
62def boot_id() -> str | None:
63 """A per-boot identifier, or ``None`` when unreadable (non-Linux, or the
64 file is hidden by an outer sandbox) — a record with no boot id is never
65 rejected for that reason alone."""
66 try:
67 value = Path("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id").read_text().strip()
68 except OSError:
69 return None
70 return value or None
71
72
73def proc_cmdline_head(pid: int) -> str | None:
74 """argv[0] of ``/proc/<pid>/cmdline``, or ``None`` when unreadable."""
75 try:
76 raw = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline").read_bytes()
77 except OSError:
78 return None
79 head = raw.split(b"\0", 1)[0].decode(errors="replace")
80 return head or None
81
82
83def proc_starttime(pid: int) -> str | None:
84 """Field 22 of ``/proc/<pid>/stat``, or ``None`` when unreadable."""
85 try:
86 stat = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read_text()
87 except OSError:
88 return None
89 _, _, rest = stat.rpartition(")")
90 fields = rest.split()
91 return fields[19] if len(fields) > 19 else None
92
93
94def proc_state(pid: int) -> str | None:
95 """The single-character state field (field 3) of ``/proc/<pid>/stat`` —
96 ``"Z"`` is a zombie: exited but not yet reaped."""
97 try:
98 stat = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read_text()
99 except OSError:
100 return None
101 _, _, rest = stat.rpartition(")")
102 fields = rest.split()
103 return fields[0] if fields else None
104
105
106def process_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
107 try:
108 os.kill(pid, 0)
109 except OSError:
110 return False
111 return True
112
113
114def is_same_process(pid: int, state: RunChildState) -> bool:
115 """Mirrors ``scheduler._is_same_process``: same kernel start time, same
116 argv[0] basename."""
117 head = proc_cmdline_head(pid)
118 if head is None:
119 return False
120 if state.starttime is not None and proc_starttime(pid) != state.starttime:
121 return False
122 if state.cmdline_head is not None:
123 return Path(head).name == Path(state.cmdline_head).name
124 return True
125
126
127def is_adoptable(state: RunChildState, *, current_boot_id: str | None) -> bool:
128 """Whether the pid recorded in ``state`` may be re-adopted as the Run
129 Child that survived a crashed orchestrator."""
130 if (
131 state.boot_id is not None
132 and current_boot_id is not None
133 and state.boot_id != current_boot_id
134 ):
135 return False
136 if not is_same_process(state.pid, state):
137 return False
138 return proc_state(state.pid) != "Z"
139
140
141def wrapper_argv(cmd: str, exit_path: Path) -> list[str]:
142 """The launch wrapper's argv. ``cmd`` and ``exit_path`` are passed as
143 positional arguments (``$1``/``$2``), never interpolated into the wrapper
144 script text, so quoting inside ``cmd`` is inert to the wrapper itself."""
145 script = 'sh -c "$1"; rc=$?; echo "$rc" > "$2.tmp" && mv "$2.tmp" "$2"'
146 return ["sh", "-c", script, "sh", cmd, str(exit_path)]
147
148
149def launch(
150 cmd: str,
151 *,
152 cwd: Path,
153 exit_path: Path,
154 out_path: Path,
155 err_path: Path,
156 preexec_fn: Callable[[], None] | None,
157 env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
158) -> subprocess.Popen:
159 """Launch one Run Child. Detached (``start_new_session=True``) so it
160 survives the orchestrator process; its exit status is never read from
161 this ``Popen`` (see module docstring)."""
162 exit_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
163 out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
164 with out_path.open("wb") as out_f, err_path.open("wb") as err_f:
165 return subprocess.Popen(
166 wrapper_argv(cmd, exit_path),
167 cwd=str(cwd),
168 stdout=out_f,
169 stderr=err_f,
170 start_new_session=True,
171 preexec_fn=preexec_fn,
172 env=env,
173 close_fds=True,
174 )
175
176
177def pidfd_open(pid: int) -> int:
178 fd = _LIBC.syscall(_SYS_PIDFD_OPEN, pid, 0)
179 if fd < 0:
180 raise OSError(f"pidfd_open({pid}) failed")
181 return fd
182
183
184class TimedOut(Exception):
185 """The command exceeded its wall-clock cap and was killed."""
186
187
188def wait_exit(
189 pid: int,
190 exit_path: Path,
191 *,
192 started_monotonic: float,
193 cap_seconds: float,
194 poll_interval: float = DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_S,
195 monotonic: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
196) -> int | None:
197 """Block until ``exit_path`` appears (returns the exit code) or the
198 **awake** cap is exceeded (raises ``TimedOut``). Returns ``None`` when
199 the process vanished with no exit file — it "died with the orchestrator"
200 (killed out from under the wrapper, e.g. by a host reboot) rather than
201 completing on its own.
202
203 Prefers ``pidfd_open`` + ``select`` (works for a process this orchestrator
204 did not fork, e.g. a re-adopted child); falls back to a plain sleep-poll
205 when ``pidfd_open`` is unavailable. The exit status always comes from the
206 exit file, never from the pidfd wait itself.
207 """
208 fd: int | None
209 try:
210 fd = pidfd_open(pid)
211 except OSError:
212 fd = None
213 try:
214 while True:
215 if exit_path.is_file():
216 text = exit_path.read_text().strip()
217 return int(text) if text else None
218 elapsed = monotonic() - started_monotonic
219 if elapsed > cap_seconds:
220 raise TimedOut(f"exceeded wall_clock_min cap of {cap_seconds / 60:.2f} minutes")
221 if fd is not None:
222 select.select([fd], [], [], poll_interval)
223 else:
224 time.sleep(poll_interval)
225 if not process_alive(pid) and not exit_path.is_file():
226 return None
227 finally:
228 if fd is not None:
229 os.close(fd)
230
231
232def kill_process_group(pid: int, *, grace_seconds: float = DEFAULT_KILL_GRACE_S) -> None:
233 """SIGTERM the Run Child's process group (it is its own session/group
234 leader, via ``start_new_session=True``), then SIGKILL after a grace
235 period if it has not exited."""
236 try:
237 os.killpg(pid, signal.SIGTERM)
238 except OSError:
239 return
240 deadline = time.monotonic() + grace_seconds
241 while time.monotonic() < deadline:
242 if not process_alive(pid):
243 return
244 time.sleep(0.1)
245 try:
246 os.killpg(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
247 except OSError:
248 pass

@@ -0,0 +1,485 @@
1"""The ``run`` recipe's executor (plan U8): declared commands as confined,
2re-adoptable Run Children, no reviewer, no coder session.
3
4Layout under ``<group_dir>/run/``::
5
6 attempt-<k>/
7 <n>.state.json # RunChildState, written at launch
8 <n>.out, <n>.err # command stdout/stderr
9 <n>.exit # exit code text, written atomically by the wrapper
10 <n>.result.json # CommandResult, written once the command settles
11 settled.json # {"outcome": "failed"|"completed", ...} once this
12 # attempt reaches a terminal outcome
13 retry-note.txt # optional operator note, consumed by the next
14 # attempt after a `retry` (see _start_attempt)
15
16A crash re-entry (the orchestrator restarted mid-command) continues the same
17attempt and re-adopts whatever pid its ``<n>.state.json`` names. An operator
18`retry` after a FAILED group's attempt was marked ``settled`` starts a new
19attempt from the first command that did not exit 0 in the previous one — or
20from command 1 when ``retry-note.txt`` contains ``--from-start``.
21"""
22

86 self.workspace: Path | None = None
87 self._heartbeat = RoundHeartbeat(
88 self.paths, self.gid, log=lambda text: log_event(self.paths, text)
89 )
90
91 # ------------------------------------------------------------- entry
92
93 async def run(self) -> GroupState:
94 self.ctx.set_state(GroupState.RUNNING)
95 self._heartbeat.start()
96 try:
97 return await self._run()
98 finally:
99 self._heartbeat.stop()
100
101 async def _run(self) -> GroupState:
102 self._heartbeat.mark_phase("worktree")
103 self.workspace = await asyncio.to_thread(self.deps.workspace_for, self.group)
104 log_event(self.paths, f"group {self.gid}: run recipe worktree ready at {self.workspace}")
105 run_dir = self._run_dir()
106 attempt_no, start_idx, results = self._start_attempt(run_dir)
107 attempt_dir = run_dir / f"attempt-{attempt_no}"
108 attempt_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
109
110 for idx in range(start_idx, len(self.args.commands)):
111 n = idx + 1
112 command = self.args.commands[idx]
113 cwd = self.workspace / command.cwd if command.cwd else self.workspace
114 try:
115 result = await self._run_command(attempt_dir, n, command, cwd)
116 except (TimedOut, _CommandDied) as exc:
117 results.append(
118 CommandResult(
119 cmd=command.cmd,
120 exit_status=124 if isinstance(exc, TimedOut) else 1,
121 duration_s=command.wall_clock_min * 60.0,
122 )
123 )
124 await self._triage_and_fail(
125 f"group {self.gid}: command {n}/{len(self.args.commands)} "
126 f"({command.cmd!r}) {exc}"
127 )
128 results.append(result)
129 self._write_result(attempt_dir, n, result)
130 if result.exit_status != 0:
131 await self._triage_and_fail(
132 f"group {self.gid}: command {n}/{len(self.args.commands)} "
133 f"({command.cmd!r}) exited {result.exit_status}"
134 )
135
136 missing_outputs = [p for p in self.args.outputs if not (self.workspace / p).exists()]
137 if missing_outputs:
138 await self._triage_and_fail(
139 f"group {self.gid}: declared outputs missing: {', '.join(missing_outputs)}"
140 )
141
142 measurements, measurements_missing = self._read_measurements()
143
144 offenders = self._porcelain_offenders()
145 if offenders:
146 await self._triage_and_fail(
147 f"group {self.gid}: git status --porcelain outside commit_paths: "
148 f"{', '.join(offenders)}"
149 )
150
151 self._heartbeat.mark_phase("merging into integration")
152 commit = await self._commit_and_merge()
153
154 summary = self._build_summary(results, measurements_missing)
155 record = RunRecord(
156 commands=results,
157 outputs=list(self.args.outputs),
158 measurements=measurements,
159 summary=summary,
160 )
161 self._write_settled(attempt_dir, "completed", summary)
162 self._register_artifact(record, commit, measurements_missing)
163 log_event(self.paths, f"group {self.gid}: run recipe completed")
164 return GroupState.COMPLETED
165
166 # --------------------------------------------------------- attempts
167
168 def _run_dir(self) -> Path:
169 return self.paths.group_dir(self.gid) / "run"
170
171 def _existing_attempts(self, run_dir: Path) -> list[int]:
172 if not run_dir.is_dir():
173 return []
174 found = []
175 for child in run_dir.iterdir():
176 if child.is_dir() and child.name.startswith("attempt-"):
177 try:
178 found.append(int(child.name.removeprefix("attempt-")))
179 except ValueError:
180 continue
181 return sorted(found)
182
183 def _start_attempt(self, run_dir: Path) -> tuple[int, int, list[CommandResult]]:
184 """Returns ``(attempt_no, start_idx, results)`` — ``results`` is
185 pre-seeded with the commands a retry is carrying forward unrun."""
186 attempts = self._existing_attempts(run_dir)
187 if not attempts:
188 return 1, 0, []
189 latest = attempts[-1]
190 latest_dir = run_dir / f"attempt-{latest}"
191 settled_path = latest_dir / "settled.json"
192 if not settled_path.is_file():
193 # Crash re-entry: continue the same attempt. Resume at the first
194 # command with no recorded result yet.
195 results: list[CommandResult] = []
196 start_idx = 0
197 for idx in range(len(self.args.commands)):
198 result_path = latest_dir / f"{idx + 1}.result.json"
199 if result_path.is_file():
200 results.append(CommandResult.model_validate_json(result_path.read_text()))
201 start_idx = idx + 1
202 else:
203 break
204 return latest, start_idx, results
205 # A settled attempt: this entry is an operator `retry`. Start a new
206 # attempt, carrying forward every command that already exited 0.
207 note_path = run_dir / "retry-note.txt"
208 note = ""
209 if note_path.is_file():
210 note = note_path.read_text()
211 note_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
212 from_start = "--from-start" in note
213 results = []
214 start_idx = 0
215 if not from_start:
216 for idx in range(len(self.args.commands)):
217 result_path = latest_dir / f"{idx + 1}.result.json"
218 if not result_path.is_file():
219 break
220 result = CommandResult.model_validate_json(result_path.read_text())
221 if result.exit_status != 0:
222 break
223 results.append(result)
224 start_idx = idx + 1
225 return latest + 1, start_idx, results
226
227 def _write_result(self, attempt_dir: Path, n: int, result: CommandResult) -> None:
228 atomic_write_text(attempt_dir / f"{n}.result.json", result.model_dump_json(indent=2) + "\n")
229
230 def _write_settled(self, attempt_dir: Path, outcome: str, detail: str) -> None:
231 atomic_write_text(
232 attempt_dir / "settled.json",
233 json.dumps({"outcome": outcome, "detail": detail}, indent=2) + "\n",
234 )
235
236 # --------------------------------------------------------- commands
237
238 def _confinement_preexec(self, cwd: Path):
239 repo_root = self.paths.repo_root
240 extra_write = []
241 if self.deps.workspace_config is not None:
242 extra_write.extend(data_layer_write_paths(repo_root, self.deps.workspace_config))
243 for entry in self.args.allow_write:
244 extra_write.append(Path(entry).expanduser())
245 policy = build_policy(
246 worktree=self.workspace,
247 claude_home=Path.home() / ".claude",
248 system_paths=None,
249 extra_write=extra_write,
250 )
251 preexec_fn, _result = landlock_preexec(policy)
252 return preexec_fn
253
254 async def _run_command(self, attempt_dir: Path, n: int, command, cwd: Path) -> CommandResult:
255 cwd.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
256 state_path = attempt_dir / f"{n}.state.json"
257 exit_path = attempt_dir / f"{n}.exit"
258 out_path = attempt_dir / f"{n}.out"
259 err_path = attempt_dir / f"{n}.err"
260 cap_seconds = command.wall_clock_min * 60.0
261
262 state: RunChildState | None = None
263 proc: subprocess.Popen | None = None
264 if state_path.is_file() and not exit_path.is_file():
265 candidate = RunChildState.model_validate_json(state_path.read_text())
266 if is_adoptable(candidate, current_boot_id=boot_id()):
267 state = candidate
268 log_event(
269 self.paths,
270 f"group {self.gid}: re-adopted run child pid {state.pid} for command {n}",
271 )
272 elif not process_alive(candidate.pid) and not exit_path.is_file():
273 raise _CommandDied("died with the orchestrator (no exit file, pid gone)")
274
275 if state is None:
276 preexec_fn = self._confinement_preexec(cwd)
277 proc = await asyncio.to_thread(
278 launch,
279 command.cmd,
280 cwd=cwd,
281 exit_path=exit_path,
282 out_path=out_path,
283 err_path=err_path,
284 preexec_fn=preexec_fn,
285 )
286 state = RunChildState(
287 n=n,
288 pid=proc.pid,
289 starttime=proc_starttime(proc.pid),
290 cmdline_head=proc_cmdline_head(proc.pid),
291 started_at=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
292 started_monotonic=time.monotonic(),
293 boot_id=boot_id(),
294 )
295 atomic_write_text(state_path, state.model_dump_json(indent=2) + "\n")
296
297 self._heartbeat_phase(n, len(self.args.commands), state, cap_seconds)
298 try:
299 exit_code = await self._await_exit(
300 state.pid, exit_path, state.started_monotonic, cap_seconds
301 )
302 except asyncio.CancelledError:
303 kill_process_group(state.pid)
304 raise
305 finally:
306 # Reap our own direct child (never a re-adopted one — this
307 # process is not its parent, so waitpid would raise ECHILD) so a
308 # long-lived orchestrator does not accumulate zombies.
309 if proc is not None:
310 try:
311 await asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait, 5)
312 except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
313 pass
314 duration = time.monotonic() - state.started_monotonic
315 if exit_code is None:
316 raise _CommandDied("died with the orchestrator (no exit file, pid gone)")
317 return CommandResult(cmd=command.cmd, exit_status=exit_code, duration_s=duration)
318
319 async def _await_exit(
320 self, pid: int, exit_path: Path, started_monotonic: float, cap_seconds: float
321 ) -> int | None:
322 while True:
323 if exit_path.is_file():
324 text = exit_path.read_text().strip()
325 return int(text) if text else None
326 elapsed = time.monotonic() - started_monotonic
327 if elapsed > cap_seconds:
328 kill_process_group(pid)
329 raise TimedOut(f"exceeded wall_clock_min cap of {cap_seconds / 60:.2f} minutes")
330 await asyncio.sleep(DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_S)
331 if not process_alive(pid) and not exit_path.is_file():
332 return None
333
334 def _heartbeat_phase(
335 self, n: int, total: int, state: RunChildState, cap_seconds: float
336 ) -> None:
337 elapsed = time.monotonic() - state.started_monotonic
338 self._heartbeat.mark_phase(f"command {n}/{total} · {elapsed:.0f}s/{cap_seconds:.0f}s")
339
340 # ------------------------------------------------------------ output
341
342 def _read_measurements(self) -> tuple[dict, bool]:
343 if not self.args.measurements:
344 return {}, False
345 path = self.workspace / self.args.measurements
346 try:
347 raw = json.loads(path.read_text())
348 except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
349 return {}, True
350 if not isinstance(raw, dict):
351 return {}, True
352 return {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if isinstance(v, (int, float, str, bool))}, False
353
354 def _porcelain_offenders(self) -> list[str]:
355 status = _git_ok(self.workspace, "status", "--porcelain").splitlines()
356 offenders = []
357 for line in status:
358 if not line.strip():
359 continue
360 path = line[3:].strip()
361 if "->" in path: # rename entries: "old -> new"
362 path = path.split(" -> ", 1)[1].strip()
363 if not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern) for pattern in self.args.commit_paths):
364 offenders.append(path)
365 return offenders
366
367 async def _commit_and_merge(self) -> str:
368 if self.args.commit_paths and _git_ok(self.workspace, "status", "--porcelain").strip():
369 _git(self.workspace, "add", "-A", "--", *self.args.commit_paths)
370 _git(
371 self.workspace,
372 "commit",
373 "-q",
374 "-m",
375 f"run({self.deps.run_id}): {self.gid} {self.group.name}",
376 )
377 try:
378 return await asyncio.to_thread(self.deps.merge_group, self.group, self.workspace)
379 except (MergeConflict, PreflightFailure) as exc:
380 await self._triage_and_fail(f"group {self.gid}: merge failed: {exc}")
381 raise RuntimeError("unreachable") from exc
382
383 def _build_summary(self, results: list[CommandResult], measurements_missing: bool) -> str:
384 parts = [f"{r.cmd!r} exit={r.exit_status} ({r.duration_s:.1f}s)" for r in results]
385 text = f"run recipe: {len(results)} command(s) — " + "; ".join(parts)
386 if measurements_missing:
387 text += " (measurements_missing)"
388 return text[:ARTIFACT_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS]
389
390 def _register_artifact(
391 self, record: RunRecord, commit: str, measurements_missing: bool
392 ) -> None:
393 store = self.deps.artifacts
394 if store is None:
395 return
396 sha256 = {}
397 for out_path in record.outputs:
398 full = self.workspace / out_path if self.workspace else None
399 if full is not None and full.is_file():
400 sha256[out_path] = hashlib.sha256(full.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
401 store.register(
402 ArtifactEntry(
403 artifact_id=self.gid,
404 group_id=self.gid,
405 tasks=list(self.group.tasks),
406 recipe=self.group.recipe,
407 paths=list(record.outputs),
408 sha256=sha256,
409 commit=commit,
410 schema="RunRecord",
411 summary=record.summary,
412 status="complete",
413 measurements=dict(record.measurements),
414 )
415 )
416
417 # --------------------------------------------------------------- triage
418
419 def _triage_prompt(self, failure_summary: str) -> str:
420 commands_block = "\n".join(
421 f"{i + 1}. {c.cmd} (cap {c.wall_clock_min}min)"
422 for i, c in enumerate(self.args.commands)
423 )
424 return Template(load_template("run_triage")).substitute(
425 group_id=self.gid,
426 group_name=self.group.name,
427 failure_summary=failure_summary,
428 commands_block=commands_block or "(none)",
429 )
430
431 async def _triage_and_fail(self, failure_summary: str) -> None:
432 log_event(self.paths, f"group {self.gid}: run failure — {failure_summary}")
433 verdict, diagnosis = "work_failure", failure_summary
434 if self.deps.triage is not None:
435 try:
436 prompt = self._triage_prompt(failure_summary)
437 result = await asyncio.to_thread(self.deps.triage, prompt)
438 verdict = result.get("verdict", "work_failure")
439 diagnosis = result.get("diagnosis", failure_summary)
440 except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 — triage is one-shot, best-effort
441 diagnosis = f"{failure_summary} (triage call failed: {exc})"
442 message = (
443 failure_summary if diagnosis == failure_summary else f"{failure_summary}\n{diagnosis}"
444 )
445 if verdict == "needs_decision":
446 response = await self._escalate_decision(message)
447 if response is not None and response.answer:
448 message = f"{message}\n[operator] {response.answer}"
449 run_dir = self._run_dir()
450 attempts = self._existing_attempts(run_dir)
451 if attempts:
452 self._write_settled(run_dir / f"attempt-{attempts[-1]}", "failed", message)
453 raise GroupFailure(message)
454
455 async def _escalate_decision(self, prompt_text: str):
456 broker, policy = self.deps.broker, self.deps.policy
457 if (
458 broker is None
459 or policy is None
460 or not policy.should_escalate(EscalationKind.CODER_BLOCKED)
461 ):
462 return None
463 request = EscalationRequest(
464 id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:12],
465 run_id=self.deps.run_id,
466 group_id=self.gid,
467 generation=self.ctx.generation,
468 kind=EscalationKind.CODER_BLOCKED,
469 prompt=prompt_text,
470 context=EscalationContext(),
471 )
472 response = await asyncio.to_thread(broker.raise_escalation, request)
473 if response is None:
474 return None
475 if response.action == HumanAction.ABORT:
476 broker.trigger_abort()
477 raise RunAbort(
478 f"operator aborted the run at group {self.gid} (run recipe needs_decision)"
479 )
480 return response
481
482
483class _CommandDied(Exception):
484 """A recorded Run Child pid is gone with no exit file — it died along
485 with a previous orchestrator process rather than completing."""
orchestrator/prompts/run_triage.md
@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
1A `run` unit in group `$group_id` ("$group_name") failed. You are not a
2coder and will not relaunch anything — diagnose only.
3
4Failure: $failure_summary
5
6Commands (in order):
7$commands_block
8
9Reply with exactly one JSON object: `{"verdict": "work_failure" | "needs_decision", "diagnosis": "<one paragraph>"}`.
10
11- `work_failure`: the command, script or environment is wrong in a way the
12 next run of this unit should fix (a bad command, a missing dependency, a
13 real bug in what the command produced). The group fails with your
14 diagnosis attached.
15- `needs_decision`: only a human can resolve this (an ambiguous requirement,
16 a product trade-off, access this run does not have). The group escalates
17 your diagnosis to the operator.

1"""Run Child launch, quoting, wait, re-adoption and kill mechanics (plan U8)."""
2
3from __future__ import annotations
4
5import os
6import signal
7import time
8
9import pytest
10
11from orchestrator.execution.run_child import (
12 RunChildState,
13 TimedOut,
14 boot_id,
15 is_adoptable,
16 is_same_process,
17 kill_process_group,
18 launch,
19 proc_cmdline_head,
20 proc_starttime,
21 proc_state,
22 process_alive,
23 wait_exit,
24 wrapper_argv,
25)
26
27
28def _launch(tmp_path, cmd, *, name="cmd"):
29 exit_path = tmp_path / f"{name}.exit"
30 out_path = tmp_path / f"{name}.out"
31 err_path = tmp_path / f"{name}.err"
32 proc = launch(
33 cmd,
34 cwd=tmp_path,
35 exit_path=exit_path,
36 out_path=out_path,
37 err_path=err_path,
38 preexec_fn=None,
39 )
40 return proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path
41
42
43def test_wrapper_argv_never_interpolates_cmd_text():
44 argv = wrapper_argv(
45 "echo hi", tmp_path_placeholder := __import__("pathlib").Path("/tmp/x.exit")
46 )
47 assert argv[0] == "sh"
48 assert argv[3] == "sh"
49 assert argv[4] == "echo hi"
50 assert argv[5] == str(tmp_path_placeholder)
51 # The script text itself never contains the command — only $1/$2 refer to it.
52 assert "echo hi" not in argv[2]
53
54
55def test_quoted_pipe_and_env_prefix_command_runs_exactly_as_written(tmp_path):
56 cmd = "FOO='a b' sh -c 'echo \"$FOO\"' | tr a-z A-Z > out.txt"
57 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, cmd)
58 code = wait_exit(proc.pid, exit_path, started_monotonic=time.monotonic(), cap_seconds=10)
59 assert code == 0
60 assert (tmp_path / "out.txt").read_text().strip() == "A B"
61
62
63def test_launch_and_wait_exit_reads_status_from_file_not_from_our_own_wait(tmp_path):
64 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "exit 7")
65 code = wait_exit(proc.pid, exit_path, started_monotonic=time.monotonic(), cap_seconds=10)
66 assert code == 7
67 assert exit_path.is_file()
68
69
70def test_wait_exit_raises_timed_out_and_process_group_can_be_killed(tmp_path):
71 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "sleep 30")
72 started = time.monotonic()
73 with pytest.raises(TimedOut):
74 wait_exit(
75 proc.pid, exit_path, started_monotonic=started, cap_seconds=1.0, poll_interval=0.2
76 )
77 assert process_alive(proc.pid)
78 kill_process_group(proc.pid, grace_seconds=2.0)
79 proc.wait(timeout=3) # reap: this test is proc's direct parent
80 assert not process_alive(proc.pid)
81
82
83def test_awake_time_cap_ignores_a_simulated_suspend_gap(tmp_path):
84 """A command with a 60-minute cap that has run 20 awake minutes is not
85 killed even though 8 hours of *wall* time have passed — the cap is driven
86 by the monotonic clock the caller supplies, which a suspend never bumps."""
87 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "sleep 0.2")
88 fake_start = 1000.0
89 calls = {"n": 0}
90
91 def fake_monotonic():
92 calls["n"] += 1
93 # Simulated: 20 minutes of awake time elapsed, cap is 60 minutes.
94 return fake_start + 20 * 60
95
96 code = wait_exit(
97 proc.pid,
98 exit_path,
99 started_monotonic=fake_start,
100 cap_seconds=60 * 60,
101 poll_interval=0.05,
102 monotonic=fake_monotonic,
103 )
104 assert code == 0
105
106
107def test_kill_process_group_terminates_process_group_leader(tmp_path):
108 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "sleep 30")
109 assert process_alive(proc.pid)
110 kill_process_group(proc.pid, grace_seconds=2.0)
111 proc.wait(timeout=3) # reap: this test is proc's direct parent
112 assert not process_alive(proc.pid)
113
114
115def test_re_adoption_finds_the_same_pid_after_a_simulated_crash(tmp_path):
116 """A live Run Child, dropped without cleanup (a simulated crash of the
117 orchestrator), is still adoptable by a freshly-built state record."""
118 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "sleep 20", name="long")
119 state = RunChildState(
120 n=1,
121 pid=proc.pid,
122 starttime=proc_starttime(proc.pid),
123 cmdline_head=proc_cmdline_head(proc.pid),
124 started_at="now",
125 started_monotonic=time.monotonic(),
126 boot_id=boot_id(),
127 )
128 try:
129 assert is_adoptable(state, current_boot_id=boot_id())
130 assert is_same_process(proc.pid, state)
131 finally:
132 kill_process_group(proc.pid, grace_seconds=2.0)
133
134
135def test_re_adoption_refuses_a_pid_reused_by_a_different_process(tmp_path):
136 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "true")
137 proc.wait(timeout=5)
138 # The pid has exited; a stale record naming a different cmdline_head must
139 # never be "adopted" as if it were still that process.
140 stale = RunChildState(
141 n=1,
142 pid=proc.pid,
143 starttime="bogus-starttime-that-will-never-match",
144 cmdline_head="sh",
145 started_at="now",
146 started_monotonic=time.monotonic(),
147 boot_id=boot_id(),
148 )
149 assert not is_adoptable(stale, current_boot_id=boot_id())
150
151
152def test_boot_id_mismatch_makes_a_recorded_pid_unadoptable(tmp_path):
153 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "sleep 5")
154 try:
155 state = RunChildState(
156 n=1,
157 pid=proc.pid,
158 starttime=proc_starttime(proc.pid),
159 cmdline_head=proc_cmdline_head(proc.pid),
160 started_at="now",
161 started_monotonic=time.monotonic(),
162 boot_id="a-different-boot-id",
163 )
164 assert not is_adoptable(state, current_boot_id=boot_id())
165 finally:
166 kill_process_group(proc.pid, grace_seconds=2.0)
167
168
169def test_zombie_state_is_not_adoptable(tmp_path):
170 """A process whose parent never reaped it is a zombie (state 'Z') — the
171 parent here is the ``sh`` wrapper itself, so instead we drive the state-Z
172 check directly against a fork()ed-and-not-waited child of this test."""
173 pid = os.fork()
174 if pid == 0: # child
175 os._exit(0)
176 time.sleep(0.2) # let the child exit and become a zombie
177 try:
178 assert proc_state(pid) == "Z"
179 state = RunChildState(
180 n=1,
181 pid=pid,
182 starttime=proc_starttime(pid),
183 cmdline_head=proc_cmdline_head(pid),
184 started_at="now",
185 started_monotonic=time.monotonic(),
186 boot_id=boot_id(),
187 )
188 assert not is_adoptable(state, current_boot_id=boot_id())
189 finally:
190 os.waitpid(pid, 0)
191
192
193def test_signal_killed_command_wrapper_still_writes_no_exit_file_until_reaped(tmp_path):
194 """A command killed by a signal before the wrapper's ``echo`` runs never
195 gets an exit file — this is the 'died with the orchestrator' path, not a
196 128+n exit code, because the whole process group (wrapper included) is
197 what gets SIGKILLed on a timeout."""
198 proc, exit_path, out_path, err_path = _launch(tmp_path, "sleep 30")
199 os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
200 proc.wait(timeout=3)
201 assert not exit_path.is_file()

@@ -0,0 +1,426 @@
1"""The `run` recipe's executor: confined Run Children, artifact registration,
2commit_paths enforcement, retry/from-start resume, and timeout/triage (plan U8).
3"""
4

70class FakeContext:
71 def __init__(self, group: Group, generation: int = 0):
72 self.group = group
73 self.generation = generation
74 self.states: list[GroupState] = []
75
76 def set_state(self, state: GroupState) -> None:
77 self.states.append(state)
78
79 def set_generation(self, generation: int) -> None:
80 self.generation = generation
81
82 def record_cure(self) -> int:
83 return 0

86def make_deps(
87 repo_root: Path,
88 run_dir: Path,
89 workspace: Path,
90 *,
91 triage=None,
92 broker=None,
93 policy=None,
94 merge_group=None,
95):
96 paths = RunPaths(repo_root, "rtest", run_dir=run_dir)
97 store = SimpleNamespace(paths=paths)
98
99 def default_merge(group: Group, wt: Path) -> str:
100 return git(wt, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
101
102 return SimpleNamespace(
103 run_id="rtest",
104 store=store,
105 workspace_for=lambda group: workspace,
106 merge_group=merge_group or default_merge,
107 triage=triage,
108 broker=broker,
109 policy=policy,
110 artifacts=ArtifactManifestStore(paths),
111 workspace_config=None,
112 )
113
114
115async def _run(deps, group, generation=0):
116 ctx = FakeContext(group, generation)
117 executor = make_executor(deps)
118 state = await executor(ctx)
119 return state, ctx

g8: recipe-docs

u9: The plan, deepen and run skills document `recipe`/`recipe_args` and the `[recipes] enabled` gate; `CONTEXT.md` gains the `run` recipe's terms; a live-tier test drives a real two-group run (a `run` unit feeding a `code` unit) end to end.

Plan section U9

U9. recipe-docs — planners, deepeners and run drivers know how to declare and drive run units, proven by one live run

  • Summary: The plan, deepen and run skills document recipe/recipe_args and the [recipes] enabled gate; CONTEXT.md gains the run recipe's terms; a live-tier test drives a real two-group run (a run unit feeding a code unit) end to end.
  • Goal: skills/orchestrator-plan/SKILL.md: the unit template gains a - **Recipe**: line (— for code, or run with its args), the task map is written as v2 when any unit declares a recipe, and the rule for choosing: a unit is run when its deliverable is what a command produces (renders, judge passes, reports, measured artifacts) or the command runs longer than 10 minutes; a coder unit keeps a Run (driver): item when the command only proves code the unit itself writes. Both the plan and deepen skills state that a coder's Run: line calls tools through PATH (uv run …), never by absolute path, because the worker Bash allowlist is anchored to PATH_PREFIXES (commit 3d93936) and denies anything else — a command needing an unusual path or binary belongs in a run unit, whose Run Child has no Bash allowlist. skills/orchestrator-deepen/SKILL.md: the sandbox sweep treats run units' commands against the Run Child profile (allow_write), and asks for wall-clock and cost figures (P5). skills/orchestrator-run/SKILL.md: preflight checks [recipes] enabled, triage of runner diagnoses, and what re-adoption looks like in run.log. CONTEXT.md: the Unit Recipe entry notes v1 ships code and run. tests/test_run_recipe_live.py builds a scratch repo, plans a run unit that writes a metrics JSON into a data dir and a downstream code unit, runs it with the real CLI, and asserts both groups complete, the code group's first prompt carried the run entry, and the bundle exports both entries.
  • Files: skills/orchestrator-plan/SKILL.md, skills/orchestrator-deepen/SKILL.md, skills/orchestrator-run/SKILL.md, CONTEXT.md, tests/test_run_recipe_live.py (new, medium)
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: U2, U7, U8
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: consumes task-map-v2
  • Verification:
    • uv run smart-mcps-orchestrate group docs/plans/2026-09-24-001-feat-unit-recipes-run-plan.md --no-spec still succeeds after the skill edits (the skills changed, the v1 reader did not).
    • The plan skill's template, pasted into a scratch plan with one run unit and marked v2, passes plan-check and group --no-spec with [recipes] enabled = ["run"].
    • Run (driver): uv run pytest -m llm tests/test_run_recipe_live.py — Pass: both groups COMPLETED, artifacts.json holds one run and one code entry, and the exported ingest.json carries both under artifacts.
    • Run (driver), optional — run it when the triage path changed or looks hard: uv run pytest -m llm tests/test_run_recipe_live.py -k triage, a scratch plan whose run unit's command exits 3 — Pass: exactly one llm/calls.json row with operation == "run_triage" for that group, whose parsed response validates as RunTriage, and the group ends FAILED (HITL off) with the diagnosis in its failure text. Structural checks only — never an assertion on the diagnosis wording.
  • Edge cases:
    • An absolute-path tool call in a coder Run: line is denied by the anchored Bash allowlist; the deepen sandbox sweep flags it and suggests uv run … or a run unit.

Group g8: recipe-docs — planners, deepeners and run drivers know how to declare and drive run units, proven by one live run

  • g6 provides u7-bundle-additive: the Run Bundle exports artifact_manifest and run_triage llm_calls rows without a schema_version bump; the runner role label.
  • g7 provides u8-run-recipe: execution/run_child.py + execution/run_executor.py — confined, re-adoptable Run Children, measurements, commit_paths merge, one-shot triage.

Downstream groups: none.

Contracts (cross-group): g8 consumes task-map-v2.

Slice: none.

What to implement

Implement unit U9. recipe-docs exactly as specified in the plan document you have as shared context (see its U9 section, its Decisions section and the Unit Recipes objective). Do not restate the plan — follow it. In summary, the group's work is: documentation for three skills plus CONTEXT.md, and one new live-tier test tests/test_run_recipe_live.py that drives a real two-group run (a run unit feeding a code unit) end to end.

The unit's Goal paragraph in the plan is binding for content:

  • skills/orchestrator-plan/SKILL.md — the unit template gains a - **Recipe**: line (— for code, or run with its args); the task map is written as v2 when any unit declares a recipe; the rule for choosing run vs a coder unit with a Run (driver): item; and the PATH-not-absolute-path rule for a coder's Run: line (worker Bash allowlist anchored to PATH_PREFIXES, commit 3d93936).
  • skills/orchestrator-deepen/SKILL.md — the sandbox sweep treats run units' commands against the Run Child profile (allow_write), asks for wall-clock and cost figures, and repeats the PATH rule.
  • skills/orchestrator-run/SKILL.md — preflight checks [recipes] enabled; how to triage a runner diagnosis; what re-adoption looks like in run.log; and how to retry a run group (see the surprise below).
  • CONTEXT.md — the Unit Recipe entry notes v1 ships code and run.

Surprise reported by another group — incorporate it into the run skill

The worker implementing U8 reported two deviations from the plan's defaults (the plan's U8 "Non-goals / must-not" explicitly permits substituting mechanism, so these are the shipped behaviour and the docs must describe reality, not the plan's illustrative default):

  1. There is no --from-start CLI flag. The plain retry CLI takes no note argument. A run group's retry note is read from <group_dir>/run/retry-note.txt, and is consumed on the next attempt. So skills/orchestrator-run/SKILL.md must tell a run driver: a bare retry on a run group resumes from the first command that did not exit 0 in the last attempt; to rerun every command from the beginning, write a note containing --from-start into <group_dir>/run/retry-note.txt before issuing retry. Do not document a retry --from-start flag or any --note argument — wiring one would require cli.py, which is outside this group's files.
  2. The executor polls with asyncio.sleep, not pidfd_open + select, so that a cancelled executor task can kill the Run Child's process group. Where the run skill describes what a live run group looks like (heartbeat phase lines, re-adoption in run.log, Ctrl-C / Observatory Stop behaviour), describe the shipped polling/cancellation behaviour; do not promise pidfd-based exit detection.

Before writing either paragraph, read the shipped code (orchestrator/execution/run_executor.py, orchestrator/execution/run_child.py) and describe what it actually does — the two notes above are a pointer, not a substitute for reading. If what you find contradicts them, follow the code and report a surprise.

Constraints

  • Touch only this group's declared files: skills/orchestrator-plan/SKILL.md, skills/orchestrator-deepen/SKILL.md, skills/orchestrator-run/SKILL.md, CONTEXT.md, tests/test_run_recipe_live.py (new).
  • The v1 reader is unchanged by this unit: existing plans and skills that emit v1 task maps must keep working. Skill edits are additive.
  • The live test is -m llm tiered and driver-run; write it so it is collected but skipped without the marker, in the style of the repo's existing live tests.
  • Follow the repo's documentation preferences: prose that a planner or driver can act on, no restatement of the plan document, no lavish formatting.

Done means

All four documents describe the run recipe accurately against the shipped U8 behaviour (including the retry-note file and the polling/cancellation semantics), the live test exists and passes when driven with the llm marker, and every verification item below holds.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the plan digest: one summary line per unit) — never another group's spec.

307
308A `run` unit (`recipe: run`) has no coder `Run:` lines to check — sweep its
309`recipe_args.commands[].cmd` entries the same way, but against the **Run
310Child profile**, not the worker profile: the worker's Landlock grants plus
311`[workspace] data_dirs` plus that unit's own `recipe_args.allow_write` list
312(`orchestrator/execution/run_executor.py::_confinement_preexec`). A command
313writing somewhere the worker profile already covers needs nothing added; a
314fixed path outside it goes in `allow_write` (never a bare `[session] extra_write_paths` entry — that config path is the worker's own, unrelated
315list); a path not knowable until the run is the same "not verifiable" case as
316above — say so rather than inventing an `allow_write` entry to guess it.
317`allow_write` rejects (at parse time) any entry equal to or containing
318`~/.claude` or `~/.claude/projects` — never propose routing around that.

199### `run` vs a coder's `Run (driver):` item
200
201Both let the plan ask for a command to execute for real, but they are
202different machines. A coder unit with a `Run (driver):` verification item is
203still `code`: a `claude` session does the work and the run-driver only runs
204the one command the worker's sandbox can't. A **`run` unit** has no coder or
205reviewer at all — the orchestrator itself launches the declared
206`recipe_args.commands` as confined Run Children (plan U8) and merges what
207they produce. Reach for `recipe: run` when the unit's whole job *is* running
208something long, expensive, or already-scripted with no code to write or
209review — rendering media, an ingest pipeline over real data, training a
210model — especially past the ~10-minute single-tool-call cap a coder's own
211turn is bound by, since a Run Child's wall-clock cap is independent of that.
212Keep it a coder unit when there is code to write, review, or iterate on, even
213if that code's own verification runs a long command.
214
215A `run` unit's `recipe_args` (validated by `RunArgs`,
216`orchestrator/recipes/run.py`) names `commands` (each a `cmd` and a
217`wall_clock_min` cap), optional `outputs` (repo-relative paths that must
218exist when the last command exits 0), optional `measurements` (a JSON file
219path whose top-level scalar keys become non-gating observations), optional
220`commit_paths` (globs — anything else in `git status --porcelain` fails the
221unit) and optional `allow_write` (extra Landlock write paths beyond the
222worker profile and the data layer; an entry equal to or containing
223`~/.claude` or `~/.claude/projects` is a parse-time error and stays that way
224— never propose widening it). A `run` unit takes no reviewer at any
225intensity and prices as its declared wall clock plus a fixed triage-token
226allowance, not file arithmetic — see `docs/orchestrator-task-map.md`'s v2
227section for the full field table and a worked example. It must not carry
228`slice` — a non-`code` unit is always its own group.
229
230Before a `run` unit reaches `group`, its recipe must be in
231`[recipes] enabled` in `.orchestrator/config.toml` — tell the human the
232config line to add; this skill never edits the config itself.
233
234### The `PATH`-not-absolute-path rule
235
236A coder's `Run:` line, and a `run` unit's `recipe_args.commands[].cmd`, both
237execute inside a confined worktree whose Bash allowlist is anchored to
238`PATH_PREFIXES` (commit `3d93936`) — a rule resolved by *name on `PATH`*, not
239by absolute path. Write `uv run scripts/foo.py`, never
240`/home/.../scripts/foo.py` or a path baked in from the planning session's own
241checkout; the worktree the command actually runs in is a different path on
242disk. A command that needs a binary or path the allowlist doesn't already
243cover is exactly the case for the deepen skill's sandbox sweep (or, if the
244whole unit's job is running that command, a `run` unit's `allow_write`) —
245never a route around it by hardcoding a path that happens to work today.

203### What a live `run` group looks like
204
205A `run` group (`recipe: run`, plan U8) has no coder, reviewer, round, or
206generation — its heartbeat instead marks phases `worktree`, then
207`command <n>/<total> · <elapsed>s/<cap>s` for each declared command in turn,
208then `merging into integration`. There is exactly one worktree for the whole
209group's lifetime (no per-generation relaunch), so `run recipe worktree ready`
210appears once and every command after it runs in that same worktree.
211
212**Re-adoption, not restart.** If the orchestrator process itself restarts
213mid-command (a crash, not a deliberate stop), the resumed run finds the
214child's pid still alive from its recorded state file and re-adopts it rather
215than relaunching — logged as `re-adopted run child pid <pid> for command <n>`
216— so a long render already in progress is never re-paid. A command that died
217along with the previous orchestrator process (no exit file, pid gone) is
218reported as a run failure for that command, not silently retried.
219
220**Cancellation is a polled kill, not an instant one.** The executor waits on
221the command by polling for its exit file roughly once a second
222(`asyncio.sleep`, not an event-driven wait) — it does not use `pidfd_open` or
223`select` to detect the exit instantly. A Ctrl-C on the driver process, or an
224Observatory Stop, cancels the executor's await; on that cancellation it kills
225the command's whole process group before propagating, so the Run Child does
226not survive the run being stopped. Expect up to roughly a second of latency
227between the stop signal and the kill, not an instant exit.

278### Triaging a `runner` diagnosis
279
280A `run` group has no coder, so `coder_blocked` above does not apply to it. On
281a failing command, missing declared output, `commit_paths` violation, or
282merge failure, the group's own one-shot `claude -p` triage call runs first
283(recorded as an `llm_calls` row, `operation: run_triage`, labeled `runner` in
284the Observatory) and returns a `verdict` of `work_failure` or
285`needs_decision`:
286
287- `work_failure` — the group goes straight to FAILED; `logs/run.log` carries
288 `group <gid>: run failure — <summary>` followed by the triage's diagnosis.
289 Read the diagnosis and the command's own `.out`/`.err` files under
290 `<group_dir>/run/attempt-<k>/` before deciding what to fix — the diagnosis
291 is a best-effort read of the tail, not a verdict to trust blindly.
292- `needs_decision` — only raised as an actual `coder_blocked`-kind escalation
293 when `[escalation] enabled = true`; with HITL off (the default) it is
294 folded straight into the same FAILED-group failure text instead, so with
295 HITL off you will never see this as a pending escalation — read it off the
296 failure text the same way.
297
298Either way, fix the underlying cause (environment, a bad command, a wrong
299`recipe_args` field, the launch branch) the same way as any other
300`coder_blocked` fix, then release and retry the group:
301
3021. `smart-mcps-orchestrate retry $RUN <gid>` (the CLI subcommand, not the
303 escalation action — a `run` group is never mid-escalation the way a coder
304 group is).
3052. A bare `retry` resumes the group's **next** attempt from the first command
306 that did **not** exit 0 in the previous attempt — commands that already
307 succeeded are not re-run. The plain `retry` CLI takes no note text or
308 `--from-start` flag as an argument. To force every command to re-run from
309 the beginning instead, write a file containing `--from-start` to
310 `<group_dir>/run/retry-note.txt` **before** issuing `retry` — the next
311 attempt reads and deletes that file itself.
3123. `smart-mcps-orchestrate resume $RUN`.
313
